title: Material Design color palette
lede: The 2014 palette of 19 hues, each in ten shades from 50 to 900 and most with four accent shades, from which Material apps took one primary and one accent.
summary: Nineteen saturated hues in numbered shades, with 500 as the primary and A200 as a typical accent. Google, 2014.

evidence.note: Read the hex values in the HTML text of the Material Design 1 color page on 28 September 2026. No image was inspected: the page draws its swatches in HTML.

styles.note: The palette sets the style’s color grammar: one bold 500 shade for the app bar, a darker 700 for the status bar, and a contrasting accent.

context: The page says: “Color in Material Design is inspired by bold hues juxtaposed with muted environments, deep shadows, and bright highlights.” [Color](https://m1.material.io/style/color.html).

The 19 hues and their 500 shades are: Red #F44336, Pink #E91E63, Purple #9C27B0, Deep Purple #673AB7, Indigo #3F51B5, Blue #2196F3, Light Blue #03A9F4, Cyan #00BCD4, Teal #009688, Green #4CAF50, Light Green #8BC34A, Lime #CDDC39, Yellow #FFEB3B, Amber #FFC107, Orange #FF9800, Deep Orange #FF5722, Brown #795548, Grey #9E9E9E, and Blue Grey #607D8B.
Each hue runs from 50 to 900. Indigo, for example, runs from #E8EAF6 to #1A237E and adds accents A100 #8C9EFF, A200 #536DFE, A400 #3D5AFE, and A700 #304FFE.

The page describes a scheme in which the primary color fills the toolbar and status bar, and a secondary color accents the floating action button. The later edition of the page names the accent a “secondary” color.
interpretation: Almost every hue has the same brightness at 500, so any two can be swapped without redesigning the screen. This is why Material apps of 2015 look like one family in many colors.
borrow: Choose one 500 shade for the app bar, its 700 shade for the top edge, and an A200 accent from a hue at least 90 degrees away on the color wheel.
